title: Boss: run your own CA
summary: Build a complete private PKI, prove it validates, rotate the intermediate, and ship the files.

steps.title: Your own CA, end to end
body: The platform team wants a private CA for internal services. You'll build it in four steps, each reusing the last.
All certificates use ECDSA P-256 and SHA-256; "now" is 1 June 2031 UTC. The namespaces are imported.
A tidy approach: write one helper that issues any certificate, then call it three times.

steps.title: One method, three certificates
prompt: Write `X509Certificate2 Issue(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? host, int fromYear, int toYear)`:
- `issuer == null` means self-signed (use `CreateSelfSigned`), otherwise sign with `issuer` and attach the new private key
- validity 1 January `fromYear` to 1 January `toYear`, UTC
- every certificate: critical Basic Constraints (`isCa`, no path limit) and a Subject Key Identifier
- CAs: Key Usage `KeyCertSign | CrlSign`; leaves: Key Usage `DigitalSignature`
- issued certificates: an AKI from the issuer, and a random 8-byte serial (`RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(8)`, with `serial[0] &= 0x7F` to keep it positive)
- when `host` is not null: SAN DNS `host` and EKU serverAuth `1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1`
starter: X509Certificate2 Issue(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? host, int fromYear, int toYear)
solution: X509Certificate2 Issue(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? host, int fromYear, int toYear)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
using var cert = req.Create(issuer, from, to, serial);
hints: Add the extensions shared by every certificate first, then the leaf-only ones under `if (host != null)`.
The AKI needs the issuer, so add it only after the `issuer == null` early return.
`using var cert = req.Create(issuer, from, to, serial); return cert.CopyWithPrivateKey(key);`
template: using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates;
{{CODE}}
var dojoRoot = Issue("CN=Platform Root", null, true, null, 2030, 2050);
var dojoInter = Issue("CN=Platform Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true, null, 2030, 2040);
var dojoLeaf = Issue("CN=orders.internal", dojoInter, false, "orders.internal", 2031, 2032);
Dojo.Eq("root is self-signed", "CN=Platform Root", dojoRoot.Issuer);
Dojo.Eq("every certificate has its key", true, dojoRoot.HasPrivateKey && dojoInter.HasPrivateKey && dojoLeaf.HasPrivateKey);
Dojo.Eq("leaf matches its host via SAN", true, dojoLeaf.MatchesHostname("orders.internal", allowCommonName: false));
Dojo.Eq("leaf is not a CA", false, dojoLeaf.Extensions.OfType<X509BasicConstraintsExtension>().Single().CertificateAuthority);
Dojo.Eq("intermediate has no SAN", false, dojoInter.Extensions.OfType<X509SubjectAlternativeNameExtension>().Any());
using var dojoChain = new X509Chain();
dojoChain.ChainPolicy.TrustMode = X509ChainTrustMode.CustomRootTrust;
dojoChain.ChainPolicy.CustomTrustStore.Add(dojoRoot);
dojoChain.ChainPolicy.ExtraStore.Add(dojoInter);
dojoChain.ChainPolicy.ApplicationPolicy.Add(new Oid("1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1"));
dojoChain.ChainPolicy.RevocationMode = X509RevocationMode.NoCheck;
dojoChain.ChainPolicy.VerificationTime = new DateTime(2031, 6, 1, 0, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Utc);
Dojo.Check("leaf validates for serverAuth through the intermediate", dojoChain.Build(dojoLeaf), string.Join(",", dojoChain.ChainStatus.Select(s => s.Status)));
Dojo.Eq("chain has three elements", 3, dojoChain.ChainElements.Count);

steps.title: The validator
prompt: `Issue` is already in the editor. Add `bool IsValidServer(X509Certificate2 leaf, string host, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)`
that returns true only when the chain validates (custom root trust, intermediates as extra, serverAuth, no revocation,
verification time 2031-06-01 UTC) **and** the leaf matches `host` without falling back to the CN.

template: using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates;
{{CODE}}
var dojoRoot = Issue("CN=Platform Root", null, true, null, 2030, 2050);
var dojoInter = Issue("CN=Platform Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true, null, 2030, 2040);
var dojoLeaf = Issue("CN=orders.internal", dojoInter, false, "orders.internal", 2031, 2032);
var dojoExpired = Issue("CN=old.internal", dojoInter, false, "old.internal", 2030, 2031);
var dojoNoSan = Issue("CN=nosan.internal", dojoInter, false, null, 2031, 2032);
var dojoOtherRoot = Issue("CN=Platform Root", null, true, null, 2030, 2050);
Dojo.Eq("good leaf", true, IsValidServer(dojoLeaf, "orders.internal", dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }));
Dojo.Eq("wrong host", false, IsValidServer(dojoLeaf, "billing.internal", dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }));
Dojo.Eq("expired leaf", false, IsValidServer(dojoExpired, "old.internal", dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }));
Dojo.Eq("CN only, no SAN", false, IsValidServer(dojoNoSan, "nosan.internal", dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }));
Dojo.Eq("look-alike root", false, IsValidServer(dojoLeaf, "orders.internal", dojoOtherRoot, new() { dojoInter }));
Dojo.Eq("intermediate not supplied", false, IsValidServer(dojoLeaf, "orders.internal", dojoRoot, new()));

steps.title: Rotate the intermediate
prompt: The issuing CA's key is suspected leaked. You must replace the intermediate **without touching the root** (so no trust store
changes anywhere) and reissue the leaf.
`Issue` and `IsValidServer` are already in the editor. Write `(X509Certificate2 NewInter, X509Certificate2 NewLeaf) Rotate(X509Certificate2 root, string host)`
that issues a new intermediate `CN=Platform Issuing CA 2` (2031 to 2040) from `root`, and a new leaf for `host` (2031 to 2032) from it.
The tests check that the new leaf validates with the new intermediate, and **fails** if a server keeps sending only the old intermediate.

var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
using var cert = req.Create(issuer, from, to, serial);
bool IsValidServer(X509Certificate2 leaf, string host, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)
(X509Certificate2 NewInter, X509Certificate2 NewLeaf) Rotate(X509Certificate2 root, string host)
solution: X509Certificate2 Issue(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? host, int fromYear, int toYear)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
using var cert = req.Create(issuer, from, to, serial);
bool IsValidServer(X509Certificate2 leaf, string host, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)
(X509Certificate2 NewInter, X509Certificate2 NewLeaf) Rotate(X509Certificate2 root, string host)
var inter = Issue("CN=Platform Issuing CA 2", root, true, null, 2031, 2040);
var leaf = Issue("CN=" + host, inter, false, host, 2031, 2032);
hints: Two calls to `Issue`: the intermediate from `root`, the leaf from the new intermediate.
Return them as a tuple: `return (inter, leaf);`
template: using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates;
{{CODE}}
var dojoRoot = Issue("CN=Platform Root", null, true, null, 2030, 2050);
var dojoOldInter = Issue("CN=Platform Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true, null, 2030, 2040);
var (dojoNewInter, dojoNewLeaf) = Rotate(dojoRoot, "orders.internal");
Dojo.Eq("new intermediate's issuer is the same root", "CN=Platform Root", dojoNewInter.Issuer);
Dojo.Eq("new leaf is issued by the new intermediate", "CN=Platform Issuing CA 2", dojoNewLeaf.Issuer);
Dojo.Eq("new leaf validates with the new intermediate", true, IsValidServer(dojoNewLeaf, "orders.internal", dojoRoot, new() { dojoNewInter }));
Dojo.Eq("server still sending the old intermediate fails", false, IsValidServer(dojoNewLeaf, "orders.internal", dojoRoot, new() { dojoOldInter }));
steps.explain: This is exactly why intermediates exist: the root, and every trust store that holds it, never changed. And it's why servers must ship the *current* chain file after a rotation.

steps.title: Ship the files
prompt: Deployment wants three strings. `Issue` is already in the editor (the tests use it). Write
`(string FullChain, string KeyPem, string RootPem) Package(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2 intermediate, X509Certificate2 root)`:
- `FullChain`: leaf PEM, `\n`, intermediate PEM, `\n` (the root is **not** included)
- `KeyPem`: the leaf's private key as PKCS#8 PEM: `leaf.GetECDsaPrivateKey()!.ExportPkcs8PrivateKeyPem()`
- `RootPem`: the root certificate's PEM, for clients to add to their trust store
The tests load `FullChain` and `KeyPem` back with `X509Certificate2.CreateFromPem` and check the result can sign.

template: using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates;
{{CODE}}
var dojoRoot = Issue("CN=Platform Root", null, true, null, 2030, 2050);
var dojoInter = Issue("CN=Platform Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true, null, 2030, 2040);
var dojoLeaf = Issue("CN=orders.internal", dojoInter, false, "orders.internal", 2031, 2032);
var (dojoFull, dojoKey, dojoRootPem) = Package(dojoLeaf, dojoInter, dojoRoot);
Dojo.Eq("full chain has two certificates", 2, dojoFull.Split("-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----").Length - 1);
Dojo.Check("key PEM is PKCS#8", dojoKey.StartsWith("-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----"), "use ExportPkcs8PrivateKeyPem()");
Dojo.Check("root PEM is not in the full chain", !dojoFull.Contains(dojoRootPem.Split('\n')[1]), "leave the root out of FullChain");
Dojo.Try("full chain + key load as a usable certificate", () =>
var dojoLoaded = X509Certificate2.CreateFromPem(dojoFull, dojoKey);
Dojo.Eq("loaded certificate is the leaf", "CN=orders.internal", dojoLoaded.Subject);
var dojoSig = dojoLoaded.GetECDsaPrivateKey()!.SignData(new byte[] { 1, 2, 3 }, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
Dojo.Eq("its key signs, and the leaf's public key verifies", true, dojoLeaf.GetECDsaPublicKey()!.VerifyData(new byte[] { 1, 2, 3 }, dojoSig, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256));
var dojoClientRoot = X509Certificate2.CreateFromPem(dojoRootPem);
Dojo.Eq("root PEM round-trips", dojoRoot.Thumbprint, dojoClientRoot.Thumbprint);
